title: Static: what belongs to the class

terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run the ticket roll here, and try your tickets from main.

tasks.title: Number every ticket
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1`, inside the class `Ticket`, write four fields: a `String passenger`, an `int age` and an `int number`, which each ticket has for itself, and a `static int issued`, one count shared by every ticket. Then write a constructor `Ticket(String passenger, int age)` that counts the ticket in `issued` and gives it the next number: the first ticket is number 1.

Check makes tickets of its own, a handful and then more, and reads each ticket's number, passenger and age, and `Ticket.issued` through the class's name.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about a field that belongs to the class.
Write the four fields: decide which one has `static` in front.
In the constructor, set the passenger and the age, count the ticket, then give it its number.
Take the `//` off the first three lines in `main` and run the file.
hints: A `static` field exists once, for the whole class, whatever the number of tickets. A field without `static` exists once per ticket.
Add one to `issued` first; after that, `issued` is this ticket's number.
In the constructor, after setting the passenger and the age: `issued++;` then `number = issued;`.

videos.title: Static and non-static fields and methods

tasks.title: Keep the adult fare in one place
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, write a constant, a `static final int ADULT_PENCE` of `320`. Then write a method `static int fareFor(int age)`: anyone under 16 pays half of `ADULT_PENCE`, everyone else all of it.

Check reads `Ticket.ADULT_PENCE` and calls `Ticket.fareFor` through the class's name, with no ticket, for ages of its own on both sides of 16. Its own code also tries to give `ADULT_PENCE` a new value, and Java must refuse. Check reads your lines for `ADULT_PENCE` inside `fareFor`.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about constants and static methods.
Write the constant with both words in front of its type.
Write `fareFor` with `static`, and work out both fares from the constant.
Take the `//` off the line that prints a child's fare and run the file.
hints: `final` means the value can never change after it is set; `static` means it belongs to the class, so `Ticket.ADULT_PENCE` reads it with no ticket.
A `static` method is called through the class's name, as `Ticket.fareFor(9)`. It has no ticket of its own, so it uses only its parameter and static fields.
`static final int ADULT_PENCE = 320;`, and in `fareFor`: `if (age < 16) { return ADULT_PENCE / 2; }`, then `return ADULT_PENCE;`.

tasks.title: Give each ticket its line
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, write `String line()`, which gives back the ticket's number, passenger and fare in the form `Ticket 4: Lachie, 160p`. It builds on Tasks 1 and 2.

Check makes tickets of its own, three at once included, and reads the line each one gives back.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about what a method without `static` can use.
Write `line` without `static`: it reads one ticket's own fields.
Get the fare from Task 2's method, with the ticket's age.
Take the `//` off the last line in `main` and run the file.
hints: `number` is this ticket's own number; `issued` is how many tickets there are so far. Only one of them belongs in the line.
A method without `static` can use the ticket's fields and also anything `static`, such as `fareFor`.
